Proposition
[Unbounded-curvature point picking, version I] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0071, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0072 1. ch18:18.12\group Spatial Point Picking

If $(\mathcal M^n,g,O)$ is complete and noncompact with $\sup _{\mathcal M} R=\infty $, there are disjoint balls $B(x_i,r_i)$, with $r_i\in (0,1]$ and $d(x_i,O)\to \infty $, such that \[ \sup _{B(x_i,r_i)}R\le 4R(x_i),\qquad R(x_i)r_i^2\to \infty . \]
Proof

\sketch Choose $y_i$ with $R(y_i)\to \infty $, and maximize $R(x)d(x,\partial B(y_i,2))^2$ on $B(y_i,2)$. If $x_i$ is a maximizer, set $r_i=\frac12d(x_i,\partial B(y_i,2))$. Maximality gives the factor-four bound and $R(x_i)r_i^2\ge R(y_i)$. Properness of scalar curvature along the chosen sequence gives $d(x_i,O)\to \infty $, and a subsequence has disjoint balls because $r_i\le 1$.

□
